handoff.summary: Construction contract: select exactly one preserved alternative. Clip: install(C) at 0, remove(C) at 7. Sleeve: detach(H) at 0, install(V) at 1, insert(S,V) at 2, withdraw(S,V) at 7, remove(V) at 8, assemble(H) at 9. Loop: detach(H) at 0, place(M) at 1, route(L) at 2, unroute(L) at 7, lift(M) at 8, assemble(H) at 9. Each must supply 4 at ticks 3–6 and remove every installed retainer by 10. Clip clears at 8 with H intact; component alternatives clear at 9 and optionally restore H at 10. Five component actions meet the hard function; restoration is the sixth. No simultaneous assemblies or pins with non-pin retention. Contrary dependency: freeing S or M through detach prevents intact-H tapping until both are free and assembled. Sleeve withdrawal frees S before sleeve clearance; loop unrouting leaves M placed. These separating actions were already proposed, not added by exchange. Initial provenance is implementation AC14-I-C1/C2/C3 from J05/J06/J07 with the full per-candidate source sets retained below; service AC14-S-C1/C2/C3 copied every action and supplied release annotations. Implementation forwarded J01–J12; service forwarded AI,J01,J02,J03,J04,J05,J06,J07,J09,J10,J12. AI supported only the intermediate-output/final-output analogy, with no additional J0 requirement. AM supplies no construction lineage here. Preserve this disagreement in evaluation focus without inventing contrary predictions, consensus, new mechanism, or a service winner. Refuse assumed Q capacity and unlisted operations. Root replays candidate actions.
